answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the wharf gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the spiral audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 20 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the jetty panel. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
